messages.subject: Precision to Variance - generic0 model
parts:
Dear INLA team,
I am confused with transformation to precision to variance in model generic0, in code below same example in inla.doc('generic0').
1) in inla.tmarginal it is right "1/exp(x)" to return right precision or variance?
2) in inla.emarginal it is right just "x" for variance?
My target is VarError with variance of erro and VarGE with variance of z.
Thanks a lot!!

require(INLA)
n=100
z=1:n
y=sin(z/n*2*pi)+rnorm(n,mean=0,sd=0.5)
data=data.frame(y=y,z=z)
Q = toeplitz(c(2,-1, rep(0,n-3),-1))
Q[1,1] = Q[n,n] = 1
Q[n,1] = Q[1,n] = 0
## Q as dense
formula1 = y ~ f(z, model="generic0", Cmatrix = Q, rankdef=1, constr=TRUE, diagonal=1e-05)
result1 = inla(formula1, data=data, family="gaussian")
summary(result1)

post.e <- inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/exp(x),result1$marginals.hy[["Precision for the Gaussian observations"]])
post.v <- inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/exp(x),result1$marginals.hy[["Precision for z"]])

VarError <- inla.emarginal(function(x) x, post.e)
VarError
VarGE <- inla.emarginal(function(x) x, post.v)
VarGE

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Precision to Variance - generic0 model
parts:
hopefully, the example below would clarify things.

> r = inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y = 1:10))
> names(r$marginals.hyperpar)
[1] "Precision for the Gaussian observations"
> m = r$marginals.hyperpar[[1]]
> m.var = inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/x, m)
> mm = r$internal.marginals.hyperpar[[1]]
> mm.var = inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/exp(x), mm)
> plot(m.var)
> lines(mm.var)


with respect to hyperparameters, its generally better to use
result$internal..... as its the marginals in the internal
parameterisation (here log(precision)), which is more gaussian like.
some accuracy can be lost when transforming back and forth, due to the
finite representation.

when using 'emarginal', then its

> inla.emarginal(function(x) c(x, x^2), m.var)
[1] 9.129009353 105.242614496

since 'm.var', is the marginal for the variance, this would be the
E(var) and E(var^2)

Best
H
